agent_trace.summary: Brain MRI commonly shows detailed gray-white differentiation, ventricular size, deep nuclei, white matter, brainstem, and cerebellum, so image artifacts may obscure these structures or mimic pathology. Common MRI artifacts in the brain include motion, susceptibility, chemical shift, aliasing, and truncation artifacts; classification depends on their appearance and location rather than on anatomy alone.

key_facts: The brain MRI should clearly depict the cerebral hemispheres, lateral ventricles, basal ganglia, thalami, brainstem, cerebellum, and periventricular white matter.
Motion artifact often causes blurring or ghosting across the image, especially in long MRI sequences.
Susceptibility artifact is common near air-bone interfaces and metallic material and can produce signal loss or distortion.
Aliasing (wrap-around) occurs when anatomy outside the field of view is projected into the image.
Chemical shift artifact typically appears at fat-water interfaces and may produce dark or bright bands.
